claims.text: Combining opinion-based prompts, instruction-based prompts, and counterfactual demonstrations reduces the memorization ratio of text-davinci-003 from 35.2% to 3.0% on Natural Questions.
Counterfactual demonstrations improve model faithfulness in knowledge conflict scenarios compared to using original factual demonstrations.
Opinion-based prompting reframes context as a narrator's statement and asks for the narrator's opinion on questions.
Larger LLMs exhibit lower memorization ratios than smaller LLMs on filtered evaluation sets in knowledge conflict scenarios.
On RealTime QA, combining opinion-based prompts and instruction-based prompts increases text-davinci-003 zero-shot accuracy on unanswerable questions from 30.6% to 87.8%.

evidence.description: reducing the memorization ratio of text-davinci-003 from 35.2% to 3.0% on natural questions.
adding counterfactual demonstrations to prompts improves faithfulness in the aspect of knowledge conflict, while using the original (factual) demonstrations leads to limited or negative effects.
Opinion-based prompts reframe the context as a narrator's statement and inquire about the narrator's opinions
We observe that MR generally decreases with increased model size, showing that larger LLMs are better at updating memorized answers based on given contexts in knowledge conflicts.
the OPIN + INSTR prompt outperforms all others on GPT-3.5, both in the zero-shot and few-shot settings, surpassing base prompts by 57.2% and 16.3% in NoAns subset accuracy

methodologies.name: Opinion-based Prompting
methodologies.description: Context is reframed as a narrator's statement and questions ask for the narrator's opinion to encourage context reliance.

methodologies.name: Counterfactual Demonstration Retrieval
methodologies.description: Retrieves counterfactual instances using RoBERTa embeddings and cosine similarity (KATE) as in-context demonstrations.

limitations.text: The method assumes the provided context is reliable and does not address situations with erroneous or conflicting retrieved contexts.
The evaluation focuses on single-step answer extraction rather than tasks requiring multi-hop reasoning over updated knowledge.
Zero-shot opinion-based prompting does not consistently improve selective prediction on smaller LLMs (0.3B-6.7B parameters).
LLMs may persist with memorized parametric facts and ignore provided contexts in retrieval-augmented setups.

future_work.text: Evaluating proposed context-faithful prompting methods on a broader range of NLP tasks including open-domain QA and summarization.
Extending context-faithful prompting techniques to multilingual datasets and non-English tasks.
